title: Venice-Selected ‘Agata the Writer,’ Starring Mia Wasikowska, Boarded by MMM Film Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description: French sales company MMM Film Sales has acquired the international rights to “Agata the Writer,” starring Mia Wasikowska, which will have its world
body:
French sales company MMM Film Sales has acquired the international rights to “Agata the Writer,” starring Mia Wasikowska, which will have its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival in the Venice Days section, in competition.

	The Australian film is directed by filmmaker and artist Kuba Dorabialski, and is produced by Alex White, best known for “Babyteeth.”

	It follows Agata, a Polish-Australian novelist who travels from Sydney to Sarajevo to write a war novel. As she gathers material for her book, she is challenged by locals who question her motives and her relationship to the history she is attempting to portray.
	

	As her creative uncertainty grows, a strange mystery unfolds when a series of provocative and obscene artworks inexplicably disappear. Through Agata’s journey, the film reveals that her novel is not about the war itself, but about the quiet, human moments of resilience that persist in its shadow, leading her to a deeper understanding of storytelling and the responsibilities that come with being a storyteller.


	The MMM Film Sales team said, “We were immediately drawn to ‘Agata the Writer’ for its unique voice and its fascinating reflection on how we engage with history and memory. Mia Wasikowska perfectly embodies the role of Agata, a writer returning to her home continent, seeking to understand and reconnect with the wounds of the recent past, and with the ways in which unresolved conflicts continue to echo in the present. Kuba Dorabialski has crafted a film that is both playful and thought-provoking, questioning the relationship between storytelling, identity and responsibility.”
	

	“Agata the Writer” is a Whitefalk Films and Produktion Productions film. Principal production funding came from Screen Australia. It is financed with support from Creative Australia and the Adelaide Film Festival Investment Fund.

	“Babyteeth,” also produced by White, had its international premiere in competition at the Venice Film Festival, winning the Marcello Mastroianni Award. The film was nominated for 13 Australian Academy (AACTA) Awards winning nine, including best film, director and screenplay. In 2021 the film was nominated for a BAFTA Award for best director, won the Australian Directors Guild Award for best direction and as well as a British Independent Film Award nomination for best international film.

	Dorabialski is an artist and filmmaker born in Wrocław, Poland, and currently based in Sydney, Australia. He has exhibited extensively in Australia and internationally and won the John Fries Award (2017) and the Fisher Ghost Art Prize (2019). In 2021 he had his first major institutional solo exhibition at Carriageworks, a single channel long form video work Connection of the Sticks, which premiered in the FLUX: Art + Film program at the Sydney Film Festival in 2023. “Agata the Writer” is his debut feature film.

schema.headline: Venice-Selected ‘Agata the Writer,’ Starring Mia Wasikowska, Boarded by MMM Film Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Alice and Steve’ Renewed for Season 2 at Disney+ and Hulu
description:
“Alice and Steve” has been picked up for a second season at Disney+ and Hulu.

	The comedy — which airs on Disney+ in the U.K. and Ireland and on Di
body:
“Alice and Steve” has been picked up for a second season at Disney+ and Hulu.

	The comedy — which airs on Disney+ in the U.K. and Ireland and on Disney+ and Hulu in the U.S. — follows Alice (Nicola Walker), who is devastated when her best friend Steve (Jemaine Clement) starts dating her 26-year-old daughter Izzy (Yali Topol Margalith). 

	“She’s going to lose her best friend and her daughter in one fell swoop,” the synopsis reads. “Alice tries everything she can to end the relationship. Unfortunately for her, Steve’s more than ready for the attack, and what begins as a perfect friendship, devolves into an all-out feud.”
	

	Variety praised the first season, with critic Alison Herman calling Walker and Clement a “hilarious” duo. “The lived-in platonic chemistry between Walker and Clement is the show’s highlight and its foundation, keeping the action anchored in something wholesome amid some abominable behavior on both sides of the friends’ growing rift,” Herman wrote. 


	“I am so thrilled that ‘Alice and Steve’ has been given a second season,” creator and writer Sophie Goodhart said in a statement. “No one will be prepared for what happens next, especially not Alice and Steve.”

	“Alice and Steve” is executive produced by Petra Fried, Sophie Gardiner and Wim de Greef, with co-executive producer Rachael Stephenson for Clerkenwell Films, which is part of BBC Studios. The series was commissioned by Lee Mason, VP of scripted at Disney+ EMEA.

	“We absolutely love ‘Alice and Steve’ — both the show and of course the two characters at the heart of Sophie’s brilliantly messy, funny and fearless exploration of friendship and love,” Fried said. “We’re thrilled to be bringing it back for a second season and can’t wait for audiences to see what Sophie has in store for our favorite frenemies.”
	

	Added Mason: “It’s been fantastic to see the rapturous reactions to ‘Alice and Steve’ from viewers at home. Sophie has created a distinctive and original comedy, striking a chord and sparking debate with audiences across the country. I’m excited to see what mayhem Sophie and Clerkenwell have in store for our titular characters after that delicious cliffhanger — but we can expect more laughs, betrayal and bad decisions in Season 2.”

schema.headline: ‘Alice and Steve’ Renewed for Season 2 at Disney+ and Hulu

title: ‘Under Salt Marsh’ Renewed for Season 2 With Rafe Spall Returning
description:
“Under Salt Marsh” is returning for a second season at Sky.

	The crime drama has been greenlit for an “as-yet-untitled second chapter” with Rafe Sp
body:
“Under Salt Marsh” is returning for a second season at Sky.

	The crime drama has been greenlit for an “as-yet-untitled second chapter” with Rafe Spall reprising his role as Detective Eric Bull, Sky announced on Wednesday. The six-episode season will pick up as Detective Bull “moves to a remote Scottish mining village sinking under the weight of its own secrets, where a murder investigation brings him closer to the truth about his own past,” according to a press release. Season 2 is set to film in Scotland in 2027.
	

	The show’s first season, which premiered in January, starred Kelly Reilly, Naomi Yang, Harry Lawtey and more alongside Spall as he investigated the mysterious death of an 8-year-old student. It became the biggest Sky Original launch since the Eddie Redmayne-starring “Day of the Jackal,” as well as Sky’s biggest entertainment title of the year to date with a 28-day audience of 2.5 million. 


	“Under Salt Marsh” hails from creator, writer and director Claire Oakley and is produced by Little Door Productions in association with Sky Studios. Alongside Oakley, writers include In-Sook Chappell, Jonathan Harbottle and Scott Graham. The series producer is Zoranna Piggott. Executive Producers are Elwen Rowlands for Little Door Productions and Oakley, with Megan Spanjian for Sky.

	“I am thrilled to be taking the series to another unique part of the U.K. where we explore a gripping mystery and unearth buried secrets,” Oakley, who teased a potential Season 2 to Variety in February, said in a statement. “Rafe Spall brought Eric Bull’s idiosyncrasies to life so brilliantly in the first series that taking his character onwards is an absolute pleasure. And I’m delighted to be continuing the partnership with Little Door and Sky.”
	

	Added Meghan Lyvers, managing director of scripted originals at Sky: “‘Under Salt Marsh’ deeply connected with our audiences, and we’re delighted to be returning to the world Claire Oakley created for a new chapter. Claire is an exceptional storyteller, with a remarkable ability to create richly drawn characters and a powerful sense of place, and we can’t wait to see where she takes audiences next. Rafe brought such complexity and humanity to Bull in the first series, and it’s fantastic to have him back at the heart of this new story. A huge thanks to Claire, Elwen and everyone at Little Door Productions for continuing to be such brilliant partners.”

	Elwen Rowlands, executive producer and CEO of Little Door, said the second season is a “brilliant new story,” adding: “It’s been hugely exciting to see audiences respond to the series’ rich sense of place, complex characters and compelling storytelling. With Rafe Spall returning as Detective Eric Bull, this new series introduces an engaging new community and mystery, while expanding the emotional and cinematic world that made the first series so special.”

schema.headline: ‘Under Salt Marsh’ Renewed for Season 2 With Rafe Spall Returning

title: Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Korea’s DRX Corp. and PT Nuon Digital Indonesia signed a strategic partnership in Jakarta to expand gaming and entertainment ties between Indonesia
body:
Korea’s DRX Corp. and PT Nuon Digital Indonesia signed a strategic partnership in Jakarta to expand gaming and entertainment ties between Indonesia and Korea, starting with an entertainment festival called DRX Homefront Indonesia and a joint game publishing initiative between the two countries.

	The agreement pairs DRX’s esports, content production and fan engagement experience with Nuon’s local distribution network, creator relationships and knowledge of the Indonesian market. The two companies plan to start by exploring three areas: live entertainment, game publishing and talent development.
	

	Indonesia’s population of more than 280 million, its mobile-first consumer base and its appetite for Korean entertainment make it a market both companies pointed to directly in unveiling the deal.


	“Indonesia is an important market for the future of entertainment in Asia,” said Can Yang, CEO of DRX. “Success in this market requires more than bringing an international brand to local audiences. It requires the right local knowledge, relationships and execution. Working with Nuon gives us the opportunity to develop experiences that reflect what Indonesian audiences want while creating stronger connections with Korea’s entertainment industry.”

	The companies will explore developing DRX Homefront Indonesia as a flagship festival in Jakarta built around gaming and entertainment, drawing in players, fans and creators from both countries. Plans on the table include competitive gaming showcases, community programs for creators, fan meet-ups and concert-style shows featuring K-pop acts.
	

	On the publishing side, the partnership will look at bringing select Korean game titles into Indonesia while helping Indonesian-developed games reach Korea. That would put DRX and Nuon in charge of everything from picking titles and adapting them for the local market to marketing, signing up players, getting the games into stores and handling payments.

	The companies also plan to bring pieces of DRX’s existing academy setup to Indonesia, with organized coaching, camps held in Korea and routes for Indonesian players to break into the region’s pro gaming circuit.

	“Indonesia’s growing gaming and digital entertainment ecosystem presents significant opportunities for collaboration with leading players from Korea,” said Chandra Tamrin, director of Nuon. “Through this partnership with DRX, we aim to connect the strengths of both markets – bringing new gaming and entertainment experiences to Indonesian audiences while creating pathways for Indonesian games, talent and creative opportunities to reach the Korean and broader regional market. This collaboration reflects our commitment to continuously expanding Indonesia’s digital entertainment ecosystem through international partnerships.”

	DRX and Nuon plan to form a joint team to map out their initial projects and how the rollout will work, with more specifics expected once those plans come together.

	The Nuon deal extends a broader push DRX has been making beyond its esports roots. The company recently detailed plans to move into K-dramas and game publishing through its subsidiary WebsCreative, including agreements around two unannounced, fully cast K-drama projects with major Korean broadcasters. Yang has described the goal as building DRX into a digital entertainment company that keeps esports as one pillar among several, with Southeast Asia named as a priority region for that growth – a strategy the Jakarta signing puts into practice.

schema.headline: Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Mandy Patinkin Named First Honorary Team Captain of USA Fencing
description:
Inigo Montoya isn’t putting down his sword just yet. 

	Almost 40 years after Mandy Patinkin expertly parried and jousted his way to defeating the s
body:
Inigo Montoya isn’t putting down his sword just yet. 

	Almost 40 years after Mandy Patinkin expertly parried and jousted his way to defeating the six-fingered man in the beloved 1987 film “The Princess Bride,” the actor is returning to the world of foils and sabers after being tapped to serve as USA Fencing’s first-ever honorary team captain for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games in Los Angeles. 


	“Fencing is a true craft, a genuine art form, a thrilling discipline. It requires every cell of your mind and body, but particularly your mind,” Patinkin said. “It’s a form of meditation. It’s not just your physical abilities that count, and they certainly do, but I think the real fun is to get inside the other person’s mind and being, and know when and where they’re going to move before your opponent even knows it.”
	

	Patinkin’s announcement comes alongside the launch of USA Fencing’s Ambassador Program, where he also serves as a member of the Ambassador Council. Created in collaboration with the International Fencing Federation and World Para Fencing, ambassadors will introduce new audiences to the sport ahead of the Games returning to American soil after more than three decades. 

	“When Mandy and I first spoke, what struck me wasn’t the movie, though we got there eventually,” said Phil Andrews, CEO of USA Fencing. “It was how deeply he understood what this sport gives people: discipline, confidence, a community and a lifetime of joy. We could not ask for a better honorary Team Captain to lead our fencers, and our sport, into a home Games in Los Angeles.”
	

	As the honorary team captain, Patinkin will make select appearances at USA Fencing events while supporting the team on their journey to the Games. USA Fencing has been making an outreach push in entertainment industry circles to raise the sport’s profile as the 2028 Los Angeles Summer Olympic Games approach.

	Patinkin trained with Olympic fencing coach Henry Harutunian and swordmaster Bob Anderson to prepare for his role in the movie destined to become a contemporary classic, “The Princess Bride,” from director Rob Reiner.

	“I can guarantee you that every competitive fencer who has ever fenced is a much better fencer than I ever was or will be,” Patinkin said. “I’m a pretend fencer, the rest of you ladies and gentlemen are the real thing and I bow down to each and every one of you. It is all of you who keep this wonderful tradition alive, and I am honored to be a small part of it.”

schema.headline: Mandy Patinkin Named First Honorary Team Captain of USA Fencing

title: COL Group, CP Group Strike 360-Degree Partnership to Grow Thailand’s Short-Form Drama Industry
description: COL Group and CP Group are teaming on a partnership aimed at building up Thailand’s short-form drama business, linking creative training, local cont
body:
COL Group and CP Group are teaming on a partnership aimed at building up Thailand’s short-form drama business, linking creative training, local content production and distribution under a single initiative. 

	The deal centers on a talent incubation program the two firms will run jointly with an academic institution in Thailand, aimed at connecting new creative talent with the short-form entertainment sector. The companies said the effort is meant to widen the pipeline of talent feeding Thailand’s entertainment industry over time.
	

	As part of the tie-up, the two companies will also work on what they’re calling a Thai Remake Collaboration, adapting select titles from COL Group’s and FlareFlow’s libraries specifically for Thai viewers. Rather than simple translation, the chosen stories will be reworked with Thai characters, settings and language, using AIGC-enabled production tools to support the localization process. COL Group is contributing its content library and short-form production know-how, while CP Group brings its local creator network and knowledge of the Thai market.


	On the distribution side, FlareFlow will get a dedicated branded corner inside Tatang by TrueID, the short-form drama app run by True Corporation, part of CP Group. Called FlareFlow Mini, the corner is set to launch in September and will house FlareFlow’s vertical-drama catalogue for Thai audiences, with new titles added weekly.

	“Building a sustainable short-form entertainment industry requires us to invest beyond content and into the next generation of Thai creative talent. We are pleased to partner with COL Group who shares this vision and brings deep global experience in the category. Together, we can connect education with real industry opportunities – from storytelling and production to AI-enabled creation and access to real world audiences – building stronger capabilities for Thai creators and a foundation for original Thai stories and IP to grow in Thailand and beyond,” said Patsakorn Laohrenu, director of business development of content & media group, CP Group.
	

	“This partnership brings together the different pieces needed to grow short-form entertainment in a meaningful way, from developing the next generation of creators to localising proven stories for Thai audiences and creating new ways for those stories to reach viewers,” added Timothy Oh, general manager of COL Group and CMO of FlareFlow. “By working with CP Group across talent, content and distribution, we hope to contribute to a stronger and more sustainable short-form entertainment ecosystem in Thailand.”

	Tatang sits within a larger CP and True Group consumer network in Thailand that touches telecoms, e-payments, retail and marketing, and the partners plan joint promotional efforts to boost visibility for FlareFlow titles in the market.

	For COL Group, the tie-up fits into a wider international growth push, pairing its content library and production know-how with a local partner that knows the market, has an established audience and brings its own creative infrastructure.

	COL Group is known as an early mover in the microdrama space across the Chinese and U.S. markets. Its FlareFlow app, one of the leading vertical drama platforms worldwide, counts more than 45 million registered users.

	CP Group is one of Thailand’s biggest conglomerates and ranks among Asia’s largest enterprise groups, with operations in 23 countries covering everything from agriculture and retail to telecoms, e-wallets, tech and media. The company has invested in China since 1979 and owns True Corporation, a leading Thai telecommunications and digital technology player.

schema.headline: COL Group, CP Group Strike 360-Degree Partnership to Grow Thailand’s Short-Form Drama Industry

title: GameSquare Pivots Livestreaming Measurement Service Stream Hatchet Into Creator Marketing Analytics Platform (EXCLUSIVE)
description: GameSquare is rebranding its gaming and esports-focused livestreaming measurement platform Stream Hatchet into Hatchet, which it describes as “the f
body:
GameSquare is rebranding its gaming and esports-focused livestreaming measurement platform Stream Hatchet into Hatchet, which it describes as “the first full-service creator matching and brand marketing analytics platform built for marketers looking to engage in youth culture with an emphasis on gaming.”

	As part of the revamp, Hatchet, which counts Electronic Arts and NASCAR among its clients, will creator analytics including discovery, campaign tracking and ROI measurement. The rebranded platform will include an AI “Smart Search” and add in data from sources like TikTok Live, Twitter/X and Instagram along with its existing livestreaming network measurements, which are calculated based on 10 years of insights, more than 50 million creators and over 30 platforms.
	

	Per GameSquare, changes coming to Hatchet include:● End-to-End operation: Data and execution in one tool that allows users to find, verify, analyze, build, and report insights all together.● Data set expansion: Hatchet can now pull from Twitch, YouTube, Kick, TikTok and over 30 platforms. Users can narrow search by audience overlap and chat sentiment with YouTube paid-vs-organic view identifications in the work, among other new descriptors.● AI integration: For the first time, there is no manual configuration required. With “AI Smart Search,” users can evolve from a passive search platform into an active intelligence engine. This tool can also proactively surface the right creators at the right time.● Creator Community: Manage your entire creator roster from one place. Brief, track, and coordinate campaigns end-to-end via a single, customizable hub with no manual tracking.
	

	The new creator marketing analytics solution aims to help brands leverage the impact of gaming on youth culture.

	“What we are doing with Hatchet is truly unique. This is not a generic tool being retrofitted to gaming. It is a full-service proposition backed by the entire GameSquare ecosystem,” GameSquare CEO Justin Kenna said. “The goal here is to help brands live and thrive at the center of a core aspect of youth culture — gaming. For comparison, we are building something that gives the same type of insights as the Nielsen ratings, but for content creators and using the highest standard that exists in the market, with more options than other platforms offer.”

	“Over the years Hatchet has developed powerful tools and data sets to move the industry past reactive discovery,” Hatchet director of product Alessandra Pinto said. “Brands and publishers need an extension of their team, one that is continuously learning from performance patterns, surfacing opportunities, and tuning itself to their needs. Hatchet is our vision as that true strategic partner to help brands move from outreach to activation and manage the full campaign life cycle.”

	See below for more from Variety’s Q&A with Pinto about revamping Hatchet.
	
		What is driving the retooling and expansion for Hatchet?	

	The creator landscape has fundamentally changed. Creators now build audiences across multiple platforms and increasingly now include gaming as well as mainstream culture. It is critical for brands to understand a creator’s full ecosystem rather than evaluate individual channels in isolation … treating those platforms as interchangeable can mean missing important differences in audience behavior and influence.

	Hatchet is expanding to give brands a more complete view of how creators, audiences and internet culture intersect, helping them identify which creators matter to specific audiences, on which platforms, and why.
	
		Can you explain how AI is used on the platform and what purpose it serves?	

	We designed Hatchet’s AI around real challenges brands/marketers face. Smart Search allows users to describe the creator they are looking for in plain language and translates that intent into search criteria across more than 50 million creators and 30+ platforms, while the Daily Dashboard feature personalizes insights based on each user’s needs.
	

	Ultimately, we see AI as a tool to help narrow enormous amounts of data into relevant insights that support better decisions. At the end of the day, the goal is not to replace human judgment but help people make better-informed choices for their campaigns.

schema.headline: GameSquare Pivots Livestreaming Measurement Service Stream Hatchet Into Creator Marketing Analytics Platform (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Italy’s RAI Cinema International Boards Edoardo De Angelis’ ‘The Fire Within You’ Ahead of Venice Launch, Reveals First Clip (EXCLUSIVE)
description: RAI Cinema International Distribution has acquired world rights to Italian director Edoardo De Angelis‘ dark tragicomedy “The Fire Within You” ahead
body:
RAI Cinema International Distribution has acquired world rights to Italian director Edoardo De Angelis‘ dark tragicomedy “The Fire Within You” ahead of its Venice competition launch.

	De Angelis, a native Neapolitan, broke out on the festival circuit at Venice in 2016 with the Naples-set conjoined twins drama “Indivisible” and subsequently opened the festival in 2023 with anti-war epic “Comandante.” He also directed Netflix’s Elena Ferrante adaptation “The Lying Life of Adults” that year. He will now be back on the Lido vying for the Golden Lion with this more intimate piece, which revolves around the impact a toxic Neapolitan mother has on her progeny. The film is based on the prizewinning autobiographical book “Il fuoco che ti porti dentro” by Italian author and editor Antonio Franchini.
	

	“Antonio left Naples many years ago and built a successful career and family life in Milan,” says the film’s synopsis. “He escaped not only from his hometown, but also from his mother Angela, a woman extreme in both her virtues and flaws: irresistible, deeply opinionated, conservative and fiercely confrontational. Now she has arrived for Christmas and seems determined to stay. What begins as a Christmas Eve dinner soon turns into an emotional battlefield, at once comic and merciless, bringing years of misunderstandings, resentment and old wounds to the surface.”

	The synopsis continues: “A fierce emotional confrontation unfolds between mother and son, but also with a stubborn capon that refuses to end up in the cooking pot; with the anticipation of a daughter who may never arrive; and with a guest as distinguished as he is unexpected. This reckoning between mother and son will forever change the meaning of their relationship. It is a love that burns like an unquenchable fire — one that no distance and no separation can ever extinguish.”
	

	“The Fire Within You” is produced by Picomedia, an Asacha Media Group Company that is part of Fremantle, with RAI Cinema. Watch an exclusive first clip from the film above.

	Below, De Angelis speask to Variety about “The Fire Within You” ahead of the film’s Venice bow.
	
		How did “The Fire Within You” originate?	

	The author of the book, Antonio Franchini, is actually a very important editor in Italy. He was following me on the publication of the novel “Comandante,” connected to my film. We had dinner in Naples, and Antonio told me about a book he was writing about his mother. I was immediately fascinated because I found so many similarities with my grandmother and with many women I’ve met in my life. Women who are strong, charismatic, incendiary. He even told me the title and I thought it was very fitting to express the feeling they elicit. Then I read it when it came out and I loved it. But it didn’t cross my mind that it could be made into a film. Then, when I found out that there was a producer who wanted to adapt it into a film, I felt the call of the wild. Because for me, to make a film, all you need is a strong character, like Angela. Obviously, then you have to build everything else. But you can make a film based on that, then the plot can be changed, the story can be rewritten.
	
		What does Angela represent for you?	

	Well, first of all, I’m fascinated by the misunderstanding surrounding the so-called archetype of the Neapolitan mother. The Italian mother who is a loving mother, a mother hen who cooks well. See, in this case, her cooking is shit. She hates her children and her grandchildren. In fact, she actually [almost] poisons them with what she cooks. And yet, this type of figure exists in the society that I grew up in: a matriarchal, male-dominated society. That seems like a bit of an oxymoron, but it’s what I grew up with. It’s a human, maternal land of many contradictions. But this type of [toxic] female figure is a widespread archetype even in other places and parts of the world. She’s so strong, it’s devastating. “The Fire Within You” is the fire that Angela carries inside. If you distance yourself from it, you’re nothing. Away from her heat, you freeze to death. If you come too close, you burn.
	
		Tell me about working with Vanessa Scalera, who plays Angela.	

	I consider the experience of working with Scalera one of the most rewarding I’ve ever had as a director. At first, we spent days rehearsing and studying each other, because I couldn’t immediately decipher an artist like her. Then there was a moment that became a dividing line. It was when I said: “Vanessa, you’re doing everything really well. But I want something else. I want you to let go; I want you to take me places you don’t even know exist.” Well, right after that, something happened between us on set. I wanted to experience how much the character’s passion pushes her, and she doesn’t even know where this will take her. It’s so strong that it’s like driving a car too fast. You don’t have time to see the road; you don’t see the curves; you’re just going like a madman. Only a crash will stop you.
	

	This was the experience of working with Vanessa. And she probably also found some common ground between her personal biography and this character. These are things that, if an actor wants to reveal to me (about themselves) I will keep them, so to speak, in a secret drawer. If she wants to be the one to say this, she will. Or maybe she won’t. But, in short, I have reason to believe that she found some common ground between her biography and this character. Some common ground that allowed her to connect with her movements, mannerisms, attitudes and tics. But none of us really knew where we’d end up.

schema.headline: Italy’s RAI Cinema International Boards Edoardo De Angelis’ ‘The Fire Within You’ Ahead of Venice Launch, Reveals First Clip (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Stephen Colbert Urges Emmy Voters to Back Jimmy Kimmel: ‘Look How Cute He Is!’
description: With Emmy voting drawing to a close, Stephen Colbert has thrown his support behind Jimmy Kimmel in the newly revamped outstanding cariety series rac
body:
With Emmy voting drawing to a close, Stephen Colbert has thrown his support behind Jimmy Kimmel in the newly revamped outstanding cariety series race, even though Colbert’s own late-night show is competing in the same category.

	In a video posted on social media, a bearded Colbert appears sitting outdoors on a windswept coastline with a tablet on his lap, introducing himself while alluding to his recent exit: “Stephen Colbert here, at the end of the world.”
	


	“You know, there’s 24 hours left in Emmy voting, and if you’re anything like me, you haven’t even started yet. So let’s get going,” Colbert said in the video.


	“Kind of a weird voting system this year, but you know, I think we can all agree that Jimmy Kimmel deserves an Emmy,” he continued. “I don’t care if you’ve never even seen his show, you know he deserves an Emmy.”

	Colbert then flips his tablet and holds it towards the camera, showing a photo of Kimmel: “Besides, look how cute he is! Anyway, please consider thinking that Jimmy deserves an Emmy. I do. I love you.”

	In endorsing Kimmel, Colbert is returning a favor. Last year, when he was competing against Kimmel for outstanding talk series following CBS’ announcement that it would cancel “The Late Show,” Kimmel mounted his own very public campaign on behalf of his rival. He put up a billboard in West Hollywood featuring himself alongside the message: “I’m voting for Stephen.” Colbert went on to win the category. 

	This year, the two hosts are once again Emmy rivals, though under a very different set of rules. The Television Academy merged the former talk and scripted variety categories into outstanding variety series, whose five nominees are “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert,” “The Daily Show,” “Last Week Tonight With John Oliver” and “Saturday Night Live.”
	

	Kimmel also just launched an unconventional — if not daring — Emmy campaign of his own. Rather than showcasing celebrity interviews or standout monologues from “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” Kimmel assembled a campaign video largely from clips of President Donald Trump repeatedly attacking him and his show.

	For Colbert, this year’s Emmys come after the end of “The Late Show” in May following an 11-year run on CBS. Its final season earned nine Emmy nominations, including outstanding variety series and outstanding writing for a variety series.

	Colbert also made a virtual appearance last week to accept the award for outstanding achievement in variety, talk or sketch from the Television Critics Association Awards.

	The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards are set for Sept. 14.

schema.headline: Stephen Colbert Urges Emmy Voters to Back Jimmy Kimmel: ‘Look How Cute He Is!’

title: ‘Tall Tales & Murder’ First Look: Ella Lily Hyland and Aidan Gillen Star in Wild Comedic Crime Drama From ‘Veep’ Director and ‘Love/Hate’ Creator (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The BBC has lifted the chaotic lid on “Tall Tales and Murder,” its upcoming dark comedic drama from “Love/Hate” creator Stuart Carolan and co-create
body:
The BBC has lifted the chaotic lid on “Tall Tales and Murder,” its upcoming dark comedic drama from “Love/Hate” creator Stuart Carolan and co-created with Emmy and DGA award winning “Veep” director Chris Addison.

	First announced last year and shot in Ireland, the wild-sounding six-part series mixes what the synopsis describes as a “Bonnie and Clyde style adventure of bent cops, kidnapping, underworld fixers (not to mention libido-enhancing horse medication bootleggers) and the dilemmas of unconventional heroes and villains with an 8th century tall tale of monks, Vikings, buried treasure and a priceless holy book.” Yes, exactly.
	

	A co-commission from BBC Northern Ireland and RTÉ in association with Screen Ireland, “Tall Tales and Murder” is produced by Avalon (“Breeders,” ‘Starstruck, “Catastrophe”) in association with Ireland-based Metropolitan Pictures (“Kin”) and will broadcast on BBC One and BBC One Northern Ireland this fall. 


	In newly-released plot details, the series will follow Bridget, played by Ella-Lily Hyland (“Black Doves,” “Towards Zero”), an unconventional nurse who works the night shift at a Dublin nursing home. She reads the old folk bedtime horror stories, arranges clandestine late night dances and euthanises them if they ask nicely.



	

					“Tall Tales & Murder” 
									Mark Sheen
	



	But into this secret world comes Paul (Casey Walsh in his first television acting role), a young man stuck stealing cars to repay a debt to crime boss Ma Baker, played by Philippa Dunne (“Amandaland,” “Derry Girls”). Paul is desperate to stay out of prison and needs a legitimate job to keep him safe, so calls on his guardian-angel-of-sorts, an irascible detective called Bunny Ryan, played by Brian Doherty (“Blackshore, Fair City”). Bunny uses his personal history with the Matron of Bridget’s nursing home, played by Aisling O’Sullivan (Raw, The Clinic), to pull in a favour — a favour that will cost him dear.
	

	On Bridget and Paul’s first shift together at the nursing home, a mysterious, comatose patient known only as Anonymous, played by Aidan Gillen (“Love/Hate,” “Game of Thrones”), wakes up and reveals he’s the long-lost gangster Grinner McNair, with a buried hoard of Celtic gold. But they’re not the only ones after it — things get complicated as vicious gangster Wesley Swanson, played by Packy Lee (“Peaky Blinders”), and his henchmen close in.

	“Tall Tales and Murder,” was filmed in the Republic of Ireland and is based on the nine-book “Dublin Trilogy” by Caimh McDonnell.

	The series was commissioned by David Crean, RTÉ head of drama, and Dermot Horan, RTÉ director of acquisitions & co-productions; and Eddie Doyle, head of content commissioning, and Jason Butler, commissioning editor, for BBC Northern Ireland. Produced by Avalon in association with Metropolitan Pictures, “Tall Tales & Murder” is executive produced by Addison, Richard Allen-Turner, Rob Aslett, Stuart Carolan and Jon Thoday for Avalon, with David McLoughlin and Catherine Tiernan for Metropolitan Pictures. Caroline Norris is series producer, Gemma O’Shaughnessy is producer and the series is directed by Addison and Neasa Hardiman. It will be distributed internationally by Avalon.

            The "Chucky" look-alike manhunt has finally come to an end, and everyone can breathe a sigh of relief ... because the freak has been scooped up the feds in Nevada!
      
    
            Zymire Hughes — who allegedly donned a Chucky style mask and scared the crap out of people in Philadelphia — was arrested Tuesday night by the United States Marshals Service in Las Vegas, according to authorities. 
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The U.S. Marshals posted a photo on X showing two of their officers taking the "Chucky" wannabe into custody after learning that he was reportedly hiding out in an apartment complex in southeast Vegas. The officers conducted surveillance inside the complex to locate Hughes and then moved in to arrest him without incident.
      

            On August 19 ... authorities issued an arrest warrant for Hughes for aggravated assault, terroristic threats, and simple assault. Police say Hughes — while stepping into his "Chucky" alter ego — terrorized people in Philly's Center City district. Surveillance video allegedly showed Hughes chasing after a jogger with his frightening mask over his face!
      
    
            While the cops identified him and got hot on his trail, Hughes skipped town and went out to Vegas, where he had ties. Now, he's cooling his heels inside the Clark County Detention Center and awaiting extradition back to Pennsylvania.
      
    
            Sorry Chucky. You lose. Let's hope there's no sequel!

            Former boxer Adrien Broner is facing a criminal trespass charge after cops say he showed up at a Florida casino despite being banned for life ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court documents, Adrien is charged with trespass in connection with an alleged incident at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Seminole Police Department report says officers were called to the casino in April 2024 over an alleged trespass. They say Adrien was issued a lifetime ban from the casino back in August 2023 ... but claim he came back anyway, leading to his arrest.
      

                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            The case has apparently dragged on for years … and recently the court issued a warrant for Adrien's arrest.
      
    
            Adrien has yet to respond to the case.
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, Adrien is facing an unrelated civil lawsuit brought by an alleged sexual assault victim. The boxer adamantly denies the accusations.

            Megyn Kelly doesn't think much of Kim Kardashian and Kanye West's parenting skills when it comes to their 13-year-old daughter North West ... and the popular podcaster is letting the world know exactly how she feels.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            Kelly sat down with Dr. Drew on Tuesday's episode of "The Megyn Kelly Show," and the two slammed Kim and Kanye for allowing North to be such a public figure at such a young age.
      
    
            Check out the clip ... Kelly kicks things off by pointing out that North is on the cover of Dazed Magazine with false teeth, blue hair, and facial piercings. 
      
    
            Kelly also made the point that North is releasing a rap album and performing onstage -- and Kim and Kanye are "rushing" to make her into a star without thinking about the downside of celebrity for many youngsters.
      
    
            Drew agreed, saying that North has bipolar disorder in her heritage -- a clear reference to Kanye. Drew also claimed, without evidence, that Kim and Kanye are parents "who have not been available" and "don't look like they're around all the time."
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Then Drew said the former power couple put North out in the public arena, which could have strong negative ramifications, likening the situation to a "guillotine."
      
    
            We reached out to Kim and Kanye's reps for comment ... so far, no word back.
